newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Morgan's future to be left open - NZ First.
newsitem.headline: Morgan's future to be left open - NZ First.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters said on Tuesday the future of MP Tukoroirangi Morgan would be left open until the Serious Fraud Office reported its findings on Aotearoa Network Television (ATN).
In a brief statement after a caucus meeting lasting more than three hours, Peters said Morgan had apologised for his recent actions.
"Mr Morgan accepts completely that he made a serious mistake in both attempting to sell his story and later misleading his party leader.
"He apologised to his colleagues and will later tender his apology to the Prime Minister," Peters and party president Doug Woolerton said in a statement.
They said the caucus discussion had been "full and frank".
There would be no news conference on the issue.
Morgan admitted last Thursday he had tried to sell an exclusive television interview for NZ$20,000 to help fund two libel actions he is involved in.
He at first denied knowledge of the attempt to Peters, prompting the party leader to issue a statement of support which he later had to retract.

Morgan has been a recurring source of embarrassment for the National-NZ First coalition government since the October 1996 election, with revelations about spending of funds from cash-strapped Maori language channel ATN, where he used to work.
The SFO inquiry into the financial affairs of ATN is widely expected to be released this week.
